scope: Pre-output criteria compatibility and design risks only. No detector, model, tokenization, translation, new corpus or unused validation v3 was executed or opened.
corpus_scope: Six original development cases plus all12 previously exposed v2 cases; historical v2 holdout labels do not make them fresh validation.
conclusion: Retaining the exact original-script text of genuine PERSON name spans is compatible with the existing written meaning criteria when all ordinary prose is translated and identities, roles and relationships remain correct. This is a design interpretation before candidate outputs, not automatic case acceptance, a relaxed criterion, or regrading of Nick/Helen.
reasoning: The six-case instructions require preserving names and distinguishable people; reasonable transliteration variants are permitted but Latin-script output is not mandatory.
The first case explicitly permits Maria to remain Latin in Greek output. The generic preservation instruction likewise does not demand target-script conversion of names.

The exposed-v2 description says reference translations illustrate faithful meaning rather than mandatory wording; its actor/ownership criteria require the same people and roles, not a mandated name alphabet.
Ordinary prose still must be translated. Protecting an article, verb, common noun or entire untranslated clause as a name would fail that requirement.
Exact source-script retention preserves name identity but is not transliteration. A resulting feature should describe its behavior accurately.
unchanged_rules: Original name substitutions remain failures; both baseline and generic-instruction follow-up remain5acceptable/1major.
Case-specific actors, owners/borrowers, conditional and negative statements, numbers/units, permissions, quotation status and full passage coverage remain independently reviewed.
Proper marker presence or exact name spelling does not establish correct actor relationships or overall translation meaning.

risks.impact: An unprotected name can still be localized or mistranslated. Name protection is not proof that every personal name was found.
An ordinary word, title, article or neighboring prose can remain in the source language. This is especially harmful when a capitalized common word is mistaken for a person.

Greek nominative, genitive and accusative mentions may have different source spellings. Restoring exact surface text can be awkward in an English grammatical role, while inventing or guessing a base form would violate the source-only design. Grade each actual output under the unchanged rules.
Do not merge similar names or infer aliases from reference answers. Per-mention provenance avoids silent Eleni/Elena conflation, but cannot by itself preserve pronoun antecedents.
Every placeholder can be present exactly once while the output reverses who sent, approved, owned or borrowed. Counts and checksums cannot validate these propositions.
Masking a personal name may remove useful gender or agreement cues. Do not add guessed gender or role annotations from a name dictionary; use only explicit source content.
Long passages require exact original-span-to-fragment mapping. A placeholder/name must not be split or silently dropped; actual complete prompt token budgets must include the protected form.

The latest standalone Krikri screen peaked at5538.5MiB RSS under6144MiB, leaving605.5MiB observed margin. An added detector is not proven to fit concurrently; loading/unloading and combined process measurements would need their own declared check.

minimum_reviewable_contract: Freeze detector/version/settings and source-only span rules before candidate outputs. No reference names, fixture-specific dictionary or reviewer criteria as runtime inputs.

For every detected mention retain original segment ID, exact code-point offsets and exact source substring. Validate bounds, non-overlap and complete reversible source reconstruction before any request.
Use collision-resistant per-mention markers with an explicit grammar; escape or reject source-marker collisions. Do not infer identity equivalence merely from similar spellings.
Preserve the declared marker multiset within each allowed source segment/fragment. Reject missing, duplicated, unknown, malformed or partially leaked markers; do not guess a repair.
Restore exact source substrings in one nonrecursive pass. Never treat restored text as a template, regex replacement program, HTML or another marker pass.
Retain the raw model response, parsed response, source-span mapping and final restored text separately so restoration cannot hide the actual model behavior.
Validate final structure and current script rules against the original unmasked source; preserve timestamps/speakers/source text unchanged.
Independently review full final propositions and target-language ordinary prose. A structural marker pass is separate from semantic acceptance.
No larger exposed-v2, unused-v3, summary, full-app, model promotion or production change follows automatically from this feasibility note.
not_claimed: No evidence yet that any chosen source-only detector finds all required names or avoids false positives.
No evidence yet that placeholders survive native generation or improve the six-case outcome.
No promise of natural transliteration, inflection, correct coreference or actor-role fidelity.
No claim that source-name preservation fixes incorrect names already present in an ASR transcript.
